A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe the same EgoDex research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A.1-A.4 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 14 trained imitation-learning models, including numerical results in Tables 2-4, data-scaling results in Figure 5 and trajectory visualizations in Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original model evaluations, scaling analyses and qualitative predictions in Section 5 and Figures 4-5.

M1.justification: The 48-dimensional actions, chunk prediction, Transformer architectures and BC/DDPM/FM policy representations remain unchanged. Current-camera-frame relative trajectories and current-only observation inputs are newly clarified details, without evidence of a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same EgoDex tabletop manipulation coverage and trajectory-prediction/inverse-dynamics benchmarks. The 194-task collection and complete task list in Appendix A.1 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the six combinations of encoder-decoder/decoder-only architectures with BC, DDPM and flow matching. The horizon, goal-conditioning and model-size comparisons also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: The fixed 99/1 split, best-of-K evaluation, prediction horizons, model sizes and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 newly specifies that policies receive no observation history; it does not report changing an existing experimental setting.

E4.justification: The same prediction-horizon, goal-conditioning, dataset-size and model-capacity analyses are retained. Figure 4 preserves its examples and trajectory overlays. The added suggestion that history may help is not accompanied by an experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Tables 2-4 and Figure 5 retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Numerical results and reported trends are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains average/final errors of 0.045/0.062 m for Dec+BC and 0.035/0.029 m with goal conditioning. Figure 4 changes brightness only, preserving the qualitative predictions.

T1.justification: The action-dimension formula in Section 4.1, prediction mappings in Section 4.2 and SE(3) annotation description in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about dataset scale and diversity, detailed pose annotations and systematic imitation-learning benchmarks. The new abstract access link does not change the existing dataset-release claim.

C2.justification: Section 6 changes hypothetical zero-shot robot deployability from 'would' to 'may' and removes 'foundation' from the world-model use case. Appendix A.3 newly suggests that observation history may improve performance. Existing scene-diversity and tracking limitations remain.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1 and A.3 clarify relative action chunks, the current camera frame and the absence of observation history. Appendix A.4 adds repository/README directions and reported availability of sample Python loading code, supplementing v1's retained direct dataset-download instructions.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 newly connects camera-frame poses to EgoMimic [15] and relative trajectories to Universal Manipulation Interface [7]. These are limited methodological attribution additions involving already-cited works; bibliography membership and the broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and phrasing corrections, expands the name used for reference [30], and adds short technical and access explanations. The section sequence, appendix organization and overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is brightened without changing its examples or trajectory overlays, while Figures 6 and 7 are reduced in size. Figure 1's caption is shortened, with corresponding text reflow. Tables and quantitative plot structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 reduces ambiguity about action coordinates and observation history in Sections 4.1 and A.3, and improves access guidance with loading-code pointers in A.4. Section 6 also qualifies speculative zero-shot transfer. These limited gains in reproducibility and interpretive precision improve the paper while its empirical evidence remains unchanged.
